proposals.before: Yang Jun parlayed Emperor Wu’s favor into a post he never deserved; Jia Mi exploited Emperor Hui’s weakness and laid the steps to ruin—so Empress Jia met death at the Yunlin Hall, and Crown Prince Yu suffered torture and murder at Hucheng.
proposals.after: Yang Jun parlayed Emperor Wu’s favor into a post he never deserved; Jia Mi exploited Emperor Hui’s weakness and laid the steps to ruin—so Empress Dao met disaster at Yunlin, and Min Huai suffered cruel abuse at Hucheng.
proposals.reason: Chinese 悼后 and 湣懷 are posthumous designations (Empress Dao; Min Huai), not the living titles Empress Jia and Crown Prince Yu used in the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: As a young man he was sent up on the commandery quota, served on Zhong Hui’s staff as West-Pacifying General, and took part in the conquest of Shu.
proposals.after: As a young man he was sent up on the commandery quota, served on the staff of Zhong Hui, General Who Garrisons the West, and took part in the conquest of Shu.
proposals.reason: 參鎮西鐘會軍事 means Yang Xiu joined Zhong Hui’s military staff; 鎮西 is Zhong Hui’s office, not Yang Xiu’s, and is Garrison-the-West rather than West-Pacifying.

proposals.before: Once Sima Yan took the throne of Wei, he raised Yang Xiu to General of the Left Guard and made him Marquis of Sweet-Dew Hamlet.
proposals.after: After the emperor assumed the kingship, he raised Yang Xiu to General of the Left Guard and made him Marquis of Sweet-Dew Hamlet.
proposals.reason: 帝即王位後 is assumption of the kingship (King of Jin), not taking the throne of Wei.

proposals.before: His heir Wang Shiwen served as General of the Right Guard and Southern Gentlemen leader, held Xuchang, and was killed by Liu Cong.
proposals.after: His heir Wang Shiwen served as General of the Right Guard and General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, held Xuchang, and was killed by Liu Cong.
proposals.reason: 南中郎將 is a general’s office (Southern Gentlemen of the Household), not an informal ‘leader’; the literal field already has the office correctly.

proposals.before: When he and Shi Chong were implicated in a plot to poison each other, Metropolitan Commandant Fu Di impeached them; the courts recommended harsh sentences, but an imperial edict let them off.
proposals.after: When he and Shi Chong were implicated in a plot to poison each other, Metropolitan Commandant Fu Zhi impeached them; the courts recommended harsh sentences, but an imperial edict let them off.
proposals.reason: 傅祗 is Fu Zhi (祗 = Zhi), not Di; the English given name is a romanization error.

proposals.before: Shi Chong and Kai were about to do a matter of zhen poison; Metropolitan Commandant Fu Di impeached them; the authorities all judged proper heavy crimes; an edict specially pardoned them.
proposals.after: Shi Chong and Kai were about to do a matter of zhen poison; Metropolitan Commandant Fu Zhi impeached them; the authorities all judged proper heavy crimes; an edict specially pardoned them.
proposals.reason: 傅祗 is Fu Zhi (祗 = Zhi), not Di; the English given name is a romanization error.

proposals.before: He inherited the marquisate of Danyang, served on a commandery staff, and was appointed assistant magistrate of Danyang.
proposals.after: He inherited the marquisate of Dangyang, was summoned as a clerk in a ducal office, and became Assistant to the Administrator of Danyang.
proposals.reason: 當陽侯 is the Marquis of Dangyang; 丹陽丞 is the separate Danyang assistantship, and 公府掾 is a ducal-office clerkship, not a commandery staff post.

proposals.before: Chu Pou, courtesy name Yeye, was the father of Empress Kangxian.
proposals.after: Chu Pou, courtesy name Jiye, was the father of Empress Kangxian.
proposals.reason: The courtesy name 季野 is Jiye, not Yeye.

proposals.before: Chu Pou, styled Yeye, was the father of Empress Kangxian.
proposals.after: Chu Pou, styled Jiye, was the father of Empress Kangxian.
proposals.reason: The courtesy name 季野 is Jiye, not Yeye.

proposals.before: Huan Yi of Qiao saw him and marked him, saying: ‘Yeye has a Spring and Autumn inside the skin.’
proposals.after: Huan Yi of Qiao saw him and marked him, saying: ‘Jiye has a Spring and Autumn inside the skin.’
proposals.reason: 季野 in the quotation should be transcribed Jiye.

proposals.before: Chu Pou argued that the secretariat must not be run by an imperial in-law and refused the post. The court instead named him General of the Left, Inspector of Yanzhou, and commander of Yan, Xu, and Langye forces with credentials, stationed at Jincheng, while he also served as interior secretary of Langye.
proposals.after: Chu Pou argued that the secretariat must not be run by an imperial in-law and refused the post. The court instead named him General of the Left, Inspector of Yanzhou, and commander of the Langye forces in Yan and Xu with credentials, stationed at Jincheng, while he also served as interior secretary of Langye.
proposals.reason: 都督兗州徐州之琅邪諸軍事 is command over Langye military affairs within Yan and Xu, not command of all Yan and Xu.

proposals.before: Twenty-nine years later, when Empress Dowager Kangxian ruled as regent, officials proposed extraordinary honors for her father: Palace Attendant, General of the Guards, and recorder of the Department of State Affairs, while he kept his credentials, command, and inspectorship.
proposals.after: Twenty-nine years later, when Empress Dowager Kangxian ruled as regent, the authorities, because Pou was the empress dowager’s father, debated adding the rite of not being a subject, and appointed him Palace Attendant, General of the Guards, and recorder of the Department of State Affairs, while he kept his credentials, command, and inspectorship.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic rendering omits 有司以裒皇太后父 and 不臣之禮, which state that the honors were argued because he was the empress dowager’s father and included the rite of not being treated as a subject.

proposals.before: With what face could he rashly advance?’
proposals.after: With what face could I rashly advance?’
proposals.reason: The sentence continues Pou’s first-person memorial (臣); the literal English wrongly switches to third-person ‘he’.

proposals.before: The realm is still unsettled and business presses; Your Majesty should lean on your chief ministers and follow the late emperors’ habit of trusting able men. Open your heart to the empire instead of elevating kin—the court and the countryside would lose heart, and the cost would be immense.’
proposals.after: The realm is still unsettled and business presses; Your Majesty should lean on your chief ministers and follow the late emperor’s habit of trusting able men. Open your heart to the empire instead of elevating kin—the court and the countryside would lose heart, and the cost would be immense.’
proposals.reason: 先帝 is singular; the idiomatic plural ‘late emperors’ is unsupported.

proposals.before: When Shi Jilong died, Pou submitted a memorial requesting to punish him; that very day martial law was declared, aiming straight at Sikou.
proposals.after: When Shi Jilong died, Pou submitted a memorial requesting to campaign against his state; that very day martial law was declared, aiming straight at Sikou.
proposals.reason: 伐之 after 石季龍死 targets the residual regime, not punishment of the already dead man.

proposals.before: Shi Hu had just died and Zhao was in chaos; two hundred thousand people crossed the Yellow River seeking Jin protection and begging for an army.
proposals.after: Shi Hu had just died and his state was in chaos; two hundred thousand people crossed the Yellow River seeking Jin protection and begging for an army.
proposals.reason: 其國 is ‘his state’; the idiomatic name Zhao is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: While He Chong wielded chief-ministerial power, He Zhun kept his rank but lived behind a humble gate, ignored public affairs, and devoted himself to Buddhist scripture and temple building.
proposals.after: While He Chong wielded chief-ministerial power, He Zhun wore a loosened sash behind a humble gate, ignored public affairs, and devoted himself to Buddhist scripture and temple building.
proposals.reason: 散帶衡門 describes loosened dress at a humble gate, not that he ‘kept his rank’.

proposals.before: He was promoted to senior clerk on Wang Dao’s left.
proposals.after: He was transferred to senior clerk on the left of the Minister of Education.
proposals.reason: Chinese 司徒左長史 does not name Wang Dao.

proposals.before: Wang Xia, courtesy name Huanzi, father of Empress Jianshun, was a cousin of Wang Shu, Grand General Who Gallops as if Flying.
proposals.after: Wang Xia, courtesy name Huanzi, father of Empress Jianshun, was a collateral paternal uncle of Wang Shu, Grand General Who Gallops as if Flying.
proposals.reason: 從叔 is a collateral uncle, not a cousin.

proposals.before: Wang Yun, styled Shuren, was the father of Empress Xiaowu Ding, son of senior clerk on the left Meng.
proposals.after: Wang Yun, styled Shuren, was the father of Empress Xiaowu Ding and the son of Wang Meng, senior clerk on the minister’s left.
proposals.reason: Literal English drops 司徒 and fuses the father’s name with the office, as if Meng were only a clerk’s label.

proposals.before: While the Prince of Kuaiji was regent, Wang Yun sent him lists: ‘This man has standing; that man has ability.’
proposals.after: While Emperor Jianwen, then Prince of Kuaiji, was assisting in government, Wang Yun sent him lists: ‘This man has standing; that man has ability.’
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 簡文帝, leaving only the princely title and losing the identification with Emperor Jianwen.

proposals.before: ’ He strove to preserve advancement and reaching, each following his direction; therefore those who did not obtain had no resentment.
proposals.after: He strove to preserve advancement, each following his direction; therefore those who did not obtain office had no resentment.
proposals.reason: Literal line begins with a stray quotation mark carried from the previous sentence and calques 進達 unnaturally.

proposals.before: Xie An said to Yun: ‘You occupy the weight of the empress’s father; you ought not lightly belittle yourself, thereby injuring timely encounter; you should follow Lord Chu’s precedent, only letting him dwell in honor and power, in affairs not handling affairs.’
proposals.after: Xie An said to Yun: ‘You occupy the weight of the empress’s father; you ought not lightly belittle yourself, thereby injuring a timely encounter; you should follow Lord Chu’s precedent, only dwelling in honor and power and not handling the affairs.’
proposals.reason: The advice is addressed to Yun; 但令在貴權於事不事耳 refers to Yun following Chu’s precedent, not a third-person him.

proposals.before: Wang Gong’s brother Wang Shuang, courtesy name Jiming, was blunt and resolute and served as Palace Attendant at the Yellow Gate and then Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: Wang Gong’s younger brother Wang Shuang, courtesy name Jiming, was forceful and upright; he served as Palace Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and then as Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: 給事黃門侍郎 is one office, not Palace Attendant at the Yellow Gate already overlapping 侍中; 弟 is specifically younger brother.

proposals.before: ’ Thereupon he greatly extended loans to them; those who relied on Yun to be saved were seven or eight in ten.
proposals.after: Thereupon he greatly extended loans to them; those who relied on Yun to be saved were seven or eight in ten.
proposals.reason: Literal line begins with a stray quotation mark left from the previous speech unit.

decisions.reason: s0014 names 悼后 and 湣懷 and 遇雲林之災 / 濫湖城之酷; the idiomatic line’s Empress Jia, Crown Prince Yu, Yunlin Hall, and ‘death’/‘torture and murder’ are not in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 悼后遇雲林之災，湣懷濫湖城之酷

decisions.reason: 參鎮西鐘會軍事 makes 鎮西 Zhong Hui’s office (General Who Garrisons the West), not Yang Xiu’s; Xiu joined Hui’s military staff.
帝即王位後 is assumption of the kingship; taking the Wei throne is 踐阼 in the next sentence, not this one.
南中郎將 is the general’s office General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, not an informal ‘leader’.
傅祗 is Fu Zhi; 祗 is Zhi, not Di.
傅祗 is Fu Zhi; 祗 is Zhi, not Di.
當陽侯, 公府掾, and 丹陽丞 are three distinct facts: Marquis of Dangyang, a ducal-office clerkship, and assistant at Danyang—not a Danyang marquisate or commandery staff post.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 襲封當陽侯，辟公府掾，為丹陽丞

decisions.reason: 字季野 is Jiye (季 + 野), not Yeye.
字季野 is Jiye (季 + 野), not Yeye.
The quoted courtesy name 季野 should be Jiye, matching 字季野.
都督兗州徐州之琅邪諸軍事 is command of Langye military affairs in Yan and Xu, not of Yan, Xu, and Langye as three coequal commands.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 都督兗州徐州之琅邪諸軍事

decisions.reason: The Chinese states 有司以裒皇太后父 and 議加不臣之禮; the original idiomatic line omits both the kinship ground and the rite of not being treated as a subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 有司以裒皇太后父，議加不臣之禮

decisions.reason: 何顏可以冒進 continues Pou’s memorial in the same 臣 voice as 臣有何勳; third-person ‘he’ misattributes the speaker.
先帝 is one late emperor, not a plural ‘late emperors’.
After 石季龍死, 請伐之 is a campaign against the remaining state, not punishment of the already dead man.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及石季龍死，裒上表請伐之

decisions.reason: 其國大亂 is ‘his state was in great chaos’; the name Zhao is not in this sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時石季龍新死，其國大亂

decisions.reason: 散帶衡門 is loosened dress at a humble gate, not that he ‘kept his rank’.
轉司徒左長史 names the office Minister of Education’s left senior clerk and does not name Wang Dao; 轉 is transfer, not promotion.
述之從叔也 makes Xia a collateral paternal uncle of Shu, not a cousin.
司徒左長史濛之子也 identifies the father as Wang Meng, senior clerk on the Minister of Education’s left; the old literal drops 司徒 and fuses Meng with the office.
時簡文帝為會稽王，輔政 names Emperor Jianwen as Prince of Kuaiji assisting in government; the original omits 簡文帝.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時簡文帝為會稽王，輔政

decisions.reason: The unit is narrative 務存進達, not quoted speech; the leading quotation mark is stray, and 不得者 are those who did not obtain advancement.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 務存進達，各隨其方，故不得者無怨焉

decisions.reason: 謝安謂蘊曰 addresses Yun with 卿; 但令在貴權於事不事耳 tells Yun to occupy honor and power without handling affairs, following Chu’s precedent, not a third person ‘him’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宜依褚公故事，但令在貴權於事不事耳

decisions.reason: 恭弟爽 is Gong’s younger brother; 給事黃門侍郎 is one office distinct from 侍中; 強正有志力 is forceful and upright, not merely ‘blunt and resolute’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 恭弟爽，字季明，強正有志力，歷給事黃門侍郎、侍中

decisions.reason: 於是大振貸之 is narrator prose after the close of Yun’s speech; the leading quotation mark is not in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 於是大振貸之，賴蘊全者十七八焉

claimRetractions.reason: s0014 calls her 悼后; the living title Empress Jia is only in the bad idiomatic English, with no replacement title of that form in the unit.
s0014 calls him 湣懷; Crown Prince Yu is only in the bad idiomatic English, with no living crown-prince title in the unit.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted repairs restore 傅祗 as Fu Zhi; the English given name Di was a romanization error.
祗 is Zhi, not Di; the given-name claim must match the restored romanization.
字季野 is Jiye; the English courtesy-name value Yeye was produced only by the bad romanization.
